common_name: Wendy Kalanchoe (Pearl Bells, Pendant Bell-Flowered Hybrid)

planting.note: Pot up rooted cuttings in a fast-draining succulent mix and set on a bright windowsill; this hanging-habit hybrid shows off best in a raised container or basket where the nodding flowers can dangle freely.

directions: This Kalanchoe manginii-type hybrid produces slender, semi-trailing stems of small rounded leaves topped with clusters of nodding, urn-shaped flowers in rosy pink tipped with pale yellow, earning it the trade name Pearl Bells. Grow in bright light with excellent drainage, watering only after the mix has dried out completely, since the fleshy stems and leaves rot quickly in soggy soil. Like its manginii parentage, it flowers most heavily after several weeks of naturally short autumn and winter days, so avoid supplemental night lighting if a full bloom display is the goal. Its cascading form is best displayed in a hanging basket or on a raised shelf rather than a standard upright pot.

planting.note: Root stem cuttings into gritty succulent mix and grow on in a hanging basket or elevated pot; the weak, trailing stems need a raised position for the dangling flowers to show to advantage.

directions: A hybrid of Kalanchoe gracilipes and K. manginii, 'Tessa' forms a loose mound of weak, trailing stems clothed in small green leaves and hung with slender, tubular, orange-red flowers from late winter into spring. Grow in bright light in fast-draining succulent mix and water only once the soil has dried fully, since the trailing stems and leaves are prone to rot in constantly damp conditions. Its sprawling, pendent habit suits a hanging basket or the edge of a raised bed far more than an upright container, where the flowers can dangle freely on display. Pinch spent flowering stems back after bloom to keep the plant tidy and encourage fuller regrowth.

planting.note: Root leaf or stem cuttings in dry, gritty succulent mix and place in bright light; this selection colors most deeply when grown lean and given strong sun.

directions: 'Cinnamon' is a selection of panda plant with longer, narrower, felted leaves that flush a warm cinnamon-brown along the tips and notched margins, a deeper coloring than the silvery-grey species form. Strong, bright light intensifies the cinnamon tint, while low light produces flatter grey-green growth with little color contrast. Water at the soil line and let the mix dry completely between waterings, since overhead watering leaves unsightly dark spots on the fuzzy foliage and encourages rot. Left unpinched it grows into a single upright, sparsely branched stem, so trim back growing tips occasionally to promote a bushier, multi-stemmed shrublet.

planting.note: Grow in a shallow container or as a groundcover in frost-free gardens, in fast-draining succulent mix; strong light brings out the pink blush along the cream leaf margins.

directions: This variegated sport of lavender scallops carries scalloped, blue-grey-green leaves broadly edged in cream-white, with the margins flushing pink to coral under bright light or drought stress. It spreads by trailing, semi-woody stems that root readily wherever they touch soil, and small plantlets sometimes form at the notched leaf edges as in other fedtschenkoi types. Grow in full sun to light shade with excellent drainage, watering only once the soil has dried out, since constantly damp mix quickly rots the fleshy leaves and stems. Because it carries less chlorophyll than the solid-green species, keep light strong and avoid deep shade, which causes reversion to weaker, less colorful growth.
